title: Find Xor-Beauty of Array
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` of length `n`. Every ordered choice of three indices `(i, j, k)`, each from `0` to `n - 1` and allowed to repeat, has the value `(nums[i] | nums[j]) & nums[k]`, where `|` is bitwise OR and `&` is bitwise AND.

Combine the values of all `n³` such triples with bitwise XOR and return the result, which is called the xor-beauty of `nums`.
notes:
## Intuition

Evaluating all `n³` triples is far too slow for `n = 10^5`, but XOR has a useful property: equal values cancel (`x ^ x = 0`). The triples come in mirror pairs with equal values, so almost everything cancels.

- Swapping `i` and `j` does not change `(nums[i] | nums[j]) & nums[k]`. When `i != j` the two triples cancel, so only `i == j` survives, leaving `nums[i] & nums[k]`.
- That expression is symmetric in `i` and `k` too, so only `i == k` survives, leaving `nums[i] & nums[i] = nums[i]`.

The xor-beauty is therefore just the XOR of all the numbers.

## Approach

1. Start `beauty` at `0`, the neutral value for XOR.
2. XOR every `num` of `nums` into `beauty`.
3. Return `beauty`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 4]`. `beauty` starts at `0`, becomes `0 ^ 1 = 1`, then `1 ^ 4 = 5` (binary `001 ^ 100 = 101`). The answer is `5`, matching the XOR of all eight triple values.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the array.
- Space: O(1): a single running value.

## Pitfalls

- The direct triple loop is O(n³), about 10^15 steps at the limit; the symmetry argument is what removes it.
- Ordered triples matter: `(0, 1, 0)` and `(1, 0, 0)` are both counted, and that is exactly why they cancel.
- Duplicate values are not removed: `[5, 5]` has xor-beauty `0`, not `5`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `beauty` | XOR of the numbers seen so far |
| `num` | the current number of `nums` |

narration.1: The triple formula collapses to an XOR of the numbers themselves, so the solution is a single pass.
narration.2: Start at 0, which leaves any value unchanged under XOR.
narration.3: Visit every number of the array once.
narration.4: Fold the number in; it is the only value of its own triple (i, i, i) that survives the cancellation.
narration.6: Every other triple cancelled with its mirror, so this running XOR is the xor-beauty.
